conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
GASTROINTESTINAL HORMONES MATRIX
                      
   GASTRIN (G-Cells) ──► Stimulates HCl & Pepsinogen secretion; increases gastric motility.
   SECRETIN (S-Cells) ──► Stimulates watery HCO₃⁻ release from Pancreas; inhibits Gastrin.
   CCK-PZ (I-Cells)   ──► Stimulates Gall Bladder contraction & Pancreatic enzyme release.
   GIP (K-Cells)      ──► Inhibits Gastric Motility; stimulates Insulin release (Incretin).
conceptBreakdown.content:
### Comprehensive GI Hormone Summary

| GI Hormone | Source Location | Primary Physiological Stimulus | Target Organ & Specific Action |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Gastrin** | G-Cells in Gastric Antrum & Duodenum | Stomach distension, peptides, vagal stimulation | Stimulates Parietal cells ($\text{HCl}$) and Chief cells (Pepsinogen); increases gastric motility |
| **Secretin** | S-Cells in Duodenal Mucosa | Acidic chyme ($\text{pH} < 4.5$) entering duodenum | Stimulates release of $\text{HCO}_3^-$-rich watery pancreatic fluid; inhibits gastric acid secretion *(First hormone discovered - Bayliss & Starling, 1902)* |
| **Cholecystokinin (CCK-PZ)** | I-Cells in Duodenal & Jejunal mucosa | Fatty acids and amino acids entering duodenum | Contracts Gall Bladder (releasing bile); stimulates Pancreatic Acini to release zymogens; relaxes Sphincter of Oddi |
| **Gastric Inhibitory Peptide (GIP)** | K-Cells in Duodenum & Jejunum | Glucose and lipids in small intestine | Inhibits gastric acid secretion and motility; acts as an **Incretin** to stimulate pancreatic $\beta$-cell insulin release |
| **Motilin** | M-Cells in Duodenum & Jejunum | Fasting state (interdigestive period) | Initiates the **Migrating Motor Complex (MMC)** to sweep undigested debris through empty gut |
